meta.title: Finnish Alphabet
meta.subtitle: The 29 letters and their sounds, then stress and long sounds (34 notes) · both directions, as two cards each
meta.desc: The Finnish alphabet and its sounds: 34 notes — the twenty-nine letters in Finnish alphabetical order, capital and small, with each one's Finnish name; then five notes on what no single letter shows: ng, the stress, the long vowel, the long consonant and the diphthong. The first deck of the Finnish collection. Finnish uses the Latin alphabet and spells close to one letter, one sound, but its letters do not all say what they say in English — y is a vowel, the French u; ä is the a of cat; j is the y of yes — and a doubled letter is a longer sound that makes another word (tuli "fire", tuuli "wind"; kuka "who", kukka "flower"). Both directions: see a letter and recall its sound, or see a sound and recall the letter, each a card with its own schedule. Every note describes the sound in English words and gives one word that shows it, with a speaker beside the letter and the word. b, c, f, g (outside ng), q, w, x, z and å belong to the alphabet but are met in loanwords and names, and their notes say so. The sounds are approximations, as every learner's alphabet gives them; where English has no equivalent — y, ö — the card says what to do instead. Sources: the standard description of Finnish spelling and pronunciation; the example words are checked against English Wiktionary, via the kaikki.org extraction (CC BY-SA 4.0).

fields.Name: aa
fields.Sound: "a" as in father, but short — doubled (aa) it is the same sound held long

fields.Name: bee
fields.Sound: "b" as in bed — only in loanwords and names

fields.Name: see
fields.Sound: a "k" or an "s", as in the language the word came from — only in loanwords and names

fields.Name: dee
fields.Sound: "d" as in dog, but softer — the tongue only taps; met mostly where a t softens inside a word (katu, kadulla)

fields.Name: ee
fields.Sound: "e" as in bed — a pure vowel, never the "ee" of see

fields.Name: äf
fields.Sound: "f" as in fun — only in loanwords

fields.Name: gee
fields.Sound: "g" as in go — only in loanwords; in Finnish words g is met only as part of ng

fields.Name: hoo
fields.Sound: "h" as in hat — and also said before a consonant, breathed out (lahti, "bay")

fields.Name: ii
fields.Sound: "ee" as in see, but short

fields.Name: jii
fields.Sound: "y" as in yes — never the j of jam

fields.Name: koo
fields.Sound: "k" as in skin, without a puff of breath

fields.Name: äl
fields.Sound: "l" as in leaf, always clear

fields.Name: äm
fields.Sound: "m" as in man

fields.Name: än
fields.Sound: "n" as in net

fields.Name: oo
fields.Sound: "o" as in British sort, but short and with the lips rounded — a pure vowel, never the "ow" of English go

fields.Name: pee
fields.Sound: "p" as in spin, without a puff of breath

fields.Name: kuu
fields.Sound: a "k" — only in foreign names and a few loanwords

fields.Name: är
fields.Sound: a rolled or tapped "r", as in Spanish or Scottish English — always said, wherever it stands

fields.Name: äs
fields.Sound: "s" as in see — never a z sound, even between vowels

fields.Name: tee
fields.Sound: "t" as in stop, without a puff of breath, the tongue against the teeth

fields.Name: uu
fields.Sound: "oo" as in food, but short, the lips rounded

fields.Name: vee
fields.Sound: "v" as in van, softly

fields.Name: kaksois-vee
fields.Sound: a "v" — in a few loanwords and old names

fields.Name: äks
fields.Sound: "ks" as in box — in loanwords

fields.Name: yy
fields.Sound: a VOWEL: the German ü or the French u — say "ee" with the lips rounded

fields.Name: tset
fields.Sound: "ts" as in cats — in loanwords

fields.Name: ruotsalainen oo
fields.Sound: an "o" — the Swedish letter, in Swedish names and a few words from Swedish

fields.Name: ää
fields.Sound: "a" as in cat — a letter of its own, never a kind of a

fields.Name: öö
fields.Sound: the German ö or the French eu: say "e" as in bed with the lips rounded

fields.Name: äng
fields.Sound: ng is one sound, the "ng" of singer held long, never with a g after it (kengät, "shoes"); nk is that sound and a k, as in think

fields.Name: paino
fields.Sound: the stress: every word is stressed on its FIRST syllable, whatever its length
fields.Example: kalakukkoa fish pie baked in a rye crust

fields.Name: pitkä vokaali
fields.Sound: a doubled vowel is the same vowel held about twice as long, and it makes another word: tuli "fire", tuuli "wind"

fields.Name: pitkä konsonantti
fields.Sound: a doubled consonant is held for longer, with a short stop before it, and it makes another word: kuka "who", kukka "flower"

fields.Name: diftongi
fields.Sound: two different vowels side by side glide into one another in one syllable, each sound kept: ie as in "ee-eh", uo as in "oo-oh"
